summary: Michigan lost 13-6 to Indiana in overtime. The defense kept it close, while turnovers and missed kicks made the offense’s limited scoring costly. Rutgers is next at 12:30 p.m. ET Saturday.

items.headline: Michigan loses 13-6 to Indiana in overtime
items.tldr: The game stayed tied through regulation before Indiana scored in overtime. The offense needs a repeatable scoring answer while the defense keeps another game within reach.

items.headline: Carr’s first start includes two lost possessions
items.tldr: A fumbled pitch and an interception gave Indiana opportunities. Watch the exchange and first passing decision before judging how far the offense can stretch the field.

items.headline: Butkowski makes two of four field-goal attempts
items.tldr: Maize n Brew notes misses from 53 and 32 yards. Inspect the entire kicking operation when a low-scoring game makes every attempt consequential.

items.headline: Michigan holds Indiana to 212 total yards
items.tldr: The Hoosiers managed 81 passing yards in the overtime win. Keep the coverage and defensive pressure connected while asking the offense to make those stops count.

items.headline: Michigan visits Rutgers at 12:30 p.m. ET on BTN
items.tldr: Saturday’s game is at SHI Stadium. The Monday preview confirms an afternoon Eastern start and the Big Ten Network broadcast.

lead.headline: Give the defense a scoring answer.
lead.body: Secure the exchange and get the first receiving option into space. Make a red-zone possession produce a deliberate finish, with the kicking operation ready when the touchdown is unavailable.

matchup.thesis: Turn a protected possession into points
matchup.question: What should fans watch in the next game?
matchup.answer: Keep the quarterback’s first read and the blocking assignment simple enough to execute together. Take the clean gain, then choose the next scoring call from the field position actually earned.

signals.title: Quarterback decisions
signals.detail: Watch the pitch, snap and first read before the extended play. Make a secure ordinary gain the starting point for the next possession.

signals.title: Red-zone execution
signals.detail: Get the route or run lane into space before adding another wrinkle. Judge the call by the clean decision it gives the quarterback near the goal line.

signals.title: Defensive continuity
signals.summary: Keep the pressure and coverage connected
signals.detail: Carry the route through the break while the front closes the pocket. A disciplined finish should keep the opponent from turning a stalled down into an escape completion.
signals.prompt: What should I watch for with defensive continuity?

signals.title: Field-goal operation
signals.detail: Watch the snap, hold, protection and contact as one operation. Give the kicker the same settled setup regardless of the previous attempt.
